Every screenshot and every parity check comes from the browser twin. Fix: wire notify -> emit("vault-changed") in src-tauri/src/lib.rs, and add one automated desktop check (WebDriver shot or an invoke smoke over the ten commands) so P6 is not the first time the invoke() path is judged.

biggestGap: No documented path for recording work that is ALREADY FINISHED — the exact case the manual opens with ("you just finished ... a piece of work") and the one CLAUDE.md mandates ("After completing real work, log it"). Recipe 1 only covers begin-to-end ("Run work start when you begin, not at the end"), grep over crates/ finds no --started-at/--finished-at/backdate flag anywhere, and work start/--help confirms none exists. Result, reproduced in the fresh agent run: WORK-0001 in the throwaway vault carries started 2026-08-18T12:09:48Z / finished 2026-08-18T12:10:13Z — a 25-second stamp on a multi-file SGP4 implementation — so following the manual literally writes a false duration into the vault, colliding head-on with the manual own rules "Do not fabricate" and "Write updates while you work, not afterwards" (a post-hoc record cannot honestly comply). A human reading the app sees 25 seconds and distrusts every record. Fix: add a ~10-line "Recording work you already finished" subsection to Recipe 1 stating plainly that started/finished timestamp the RECORDING, not the work, and instructing the agent to put the real timeline and the per-step history in ## Outcome; or add --started-at/--finished-at to work start / work done and document them in the command reference.

biggestGap: One auditable schema contradiction, and it is the load-bearing fact of BUG-0006. WORK-0002 update 2026-07-29T14:30Z states "the list endpoint filters with status=pending|in_flight|succeeded|dead, not state, and the values are exactly the strings stored in the deliveries.status column" — i.e. quill documents `dead` on 29 July and claims present-tense parity with the DB column. But WORK-0005 only adds the `dead` value to deliveries.status in migration 0005 on ~5-6 Aug, and BUG-0006 (report + resolution + GROUND_TRUTH thread 3) pins its entire root cause on the opposite: "There is no `dead` in the document", the frozen enum was [pending, in_flight, succeeded, failed], and `failed` is the leftover. A grader reading WORK-0002 then BUG-0006 sees quill contradict quill about the same artifact. The seam is narrow — BUG-0006 repro step 1 is GET /v1/deliveries?status=dead succeeding, so the query-parameter enum and the Delivery.status response-schema enum can be read as two different enums that drifted, and WORK-0004 tests "all five statuses" which only makes sense if both failed and dead existed client-side — but no record says that, and BUG-0006 explicitly denies `dead` is in the document at all. One-word fix: change `dead` to `failed` in WORK-0002 update 1, which also removes the anachronism of documenting a status a week before the migration creates it.

biggestGap: [design] The work-list row has no responsive rule, so the record title — the only thing that identifies a row — is the first and only thing sacrificed as the window narrows: .work-row-title is the sole flex:1 child while the tag chips, the 152px agent column and the 58px timestamp are all flex:none, and src/styles/app.css contains exactly two @media blocks (1100px for .detail-layout, 820px for .sidebar) and none for the row. Measured on /p/relay/work by counting elements whose scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth: 1600px 1/12 titles clipped, 1440px (the Tauri default window in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) 1/12, 1366px 3/12, 1280px 9/12 with the worst row showing 68% of its title, 1152px 12/12 at 45%, and 960px — the app's own declared minWidth — 12/12 with the worst row showing 2%: WORK-0010 renders as the single glyph "T." while "observability kubernetes autoscaling +1" beside it keeps every pixel. Linear drops labels and keeps titles at that width; here a supported window size makes the list unreadable. Fix: below ~1200px of row width drop the tag chips first and the agent name to its avatar, and give .work-row-title a min-width so it can never fall under ~30 characters.

Agents add them with agentmon work update WORK-0012 --message"; a stubbed empty project gives the designed "No work recorded yet" state with the real start command. TRUNCATION AUDIT: I walked all 18 work records (12 relay + 6 agent-monitoring) at 1600px checking every clipping element — zero clipped nodes, zero horizontal overflow, zero horizontally scrolling code blocks, so the builder's "nothing ellipsised" claim is true for today's data; it is data-dependent though — a stubbed record with 60-character paths ellipsises the filename itself in the files card ("...very-long-runbook-name-f..."), and the same stub proves a long title is handled well (the id drops to its own line instead of trailing the last word). SECOND-ORDER GAPS, none of which flips a pairing: (a) the same facts are stated three and four times on one screen — finished date in the byline, in the fact strip and in the rail; duration in the strip, the rail and the timeline terminator; 5 of the 6 rows in the RECORD rail card are already in the strip 400px away (only Last activity is new), and on the list the "12 records - 2 in progress" meta repeats what the segmented tabs already say; Linear states each fact once, in the place with the most context; (b) the agent and tag filters are native <select> elements, so their popups will be OS-drawn inside a Linear-grade toolbar; (c) header ref chips are bare ids with no title anywhere on the page, where a PR page shows linked-issue titles; (d) the segment counts ("Done 9") are computed over the unfiltered set, so with agent=quill selected the tabs still say 9 while 2 rows show; (e) substring search means "live" matches "delivery" and returns 6 of 12 rows; (f) below 1100px the contents rail stacks under a 4000px article, where a table of contents is dead weight; (g) update cards attribute every note to the record's agent (the schema has no per-update author) — harmless today, since all 85 relay events have actor == the worklog agent, which I checked. Detail-page responsiveness is otherwise good: at 960x620 the fact strip wraps, the rail stacks, and nothing clips.

biggestGap: [comprehension] No core fact was lost, but the markdown renderer prints a number the vault does not contain, and only on-page redundancy saved the reader. WORK-0005 update 1 wraps as “...receiver returns 503 for three hours, then’ / ‘200. Without jitter, ...”; src/lib/markdown.tsx lets any “<digits>.” line interrupt an open paragraph (parseBlocks: the list guard at line 146 plus the bullet match at line 110) and then emits a bare <ol> (line 257), so the literal 200 — the status the receiver returns after recovery — is deleted from the screen and replaced by a fabricated “1.”, and one sentence is split into paragraph + list item + paragraph. The reader called it the single worst thing on the page and recovered “503 for three hours then 200” only from the Outcome parenthetical; any record whose wrapped line begins with a number (200., 503., 2026.) is silently rewritten the same way. Fix: (a) allow an ordered marker to interrupt an open paragraph only when the number is 1 (CommonMark), otherwise treat the line as paragraph continuation; (b) when a list legitimately starts at N, render <ol start={N}> so a source number can never be replaced; (c) recurse inline() inside <strong>/<em> (line 204) so follow-up 1 stops printing literal backticks around `Retry-After`. Second gap: refs render as one bare accent chip inside the tag row (WORK-0001 — no relationship word, no title) and there is no incoming-ref area, although BUG-0003, BUG-0006 and BUG-0008 all ref WORK-0005 — give refs a labelled Related block with record titles, shown in both directions, so a reader can see that the follow-ups became BUG-0008 and WORK-0011.
notes: comprehension: PASS. Read GROUND_TRUTH.md lines 101-114 (the WORK-0005 bullets), the full record vault/projects/relay/worklogs/WORK-0005.md (162 lines), the exact artifact the reader saw (progress/critic-p2-comp/work-detail-full.png, 2400x5589, plus crops r4/r5), and src/lib/markdown.tsx, so the readability claims were adjudicated rather than taken on trust. COVERAGE, item by item. WHAT 5/5 with correct detail: retry.rs (classify + next_attempt_at; ladder 10s/45s/3m/15m/1h/6h/24h; eight attempts ending ~31h after the first; +/-20% uniform jitter on every step), migration 0005 (dead_letters table + dead value on deliveries.status), dlq.rs (last status, last error, attempt count, in the same transaction that sets status=dead), POST /v1/deliveries/{id}/replay (new row, replay_of, 202 with the new id), scripts/drain-dlq.sh (concurrency cap, prints the plan unless --yes). WHY: fixed 60s retry wrong in both directions (gives up before a deploy finishes, hammers a dead endpoint sixty times an hour); short at the start / long at the end with the rolling-deploy and Friday-TLS reasons; jitter justified by correlated outages — 4,300 deliveries due inside the same 900ms window, recovery burst of 4,300 requests in under a second, named as the retry policy becoming the customer's second outage; both rejected alternatives with their reasons (2^n: early steps too tight to survive a restart, late steps unquotable in a support conversation, a ladder is a table a customer can plan around; infinite retry with an age cap: still retrying, 4 days in, is not actionable). HOW: const [Duration; 7] with the strictly-ascending debug_assert; 408/429/5xx plus connection/DNS/TLS/timeout retry; 410 Gone terminal immediately with the decommissioned-endpoint reason; other 4xx terminal with the identical-bytes reason; jitter applied at scheduling, not at claim, so the spread lands in next_attempt_at; replay creates a new delivery with replay_of instead of resetting the original, because the original timeline is the evidence someone read before replaying — the reader even caught that update 2 records the mid-work reversal (resetting was the first draft and it is wrong). VERIFICATION/OUTCOME (record is done, so graded): 4,300-delivery synthetic outage with the receiver returning 503 for three hours then 200; no-jitter 900ms bunching at every step; +/-20% spreading the same backlog over 4m48s at the 24h step with never more than 40 concurrent; cargo test --workspace 58 passed; the ladder strict-ascent/total-span test; dlq_moves_exhausted_delivery_once running two workers against the same exhausted delivery; staging dry run of 61 dead letters printing 61 planned replays and creating nothing; and the 410-from-staging grounding (8 pointless requests per delivery). FOLLOW-UPS 3/3 (Retry-After ignored, no per-endpoint circuit breaker, attempt rows accumulate). NO MATERIAL MISSTATEMENT anywhere in the reconstruction — every number, path, symbol name and date I checked matches the record. Two reader complaints are not the page's fault: the 2xx/3xx-other-than-the-success-range sentence is the record's own wording rendered faithfully (r5.png shows those code spans correct), and drain-dlq.sh missing from the WHAT bullets is the record's own asymmetry (frontmatter files: lists 5, ## What describes 4) — the page still shows the file in FILES TOUCHED, update 2 and the Outcome, and the reader got it and said so. TRUNCATION AUDIT: none. The full-page render ends on follow-up 3 exactly where the record ends; no clipped or cut-off content; the reconstruction's own final sentence stops mid-word at the writer's output limit, not the screen's. The two rendering defects the reader reported are real and I reproduced them in source: the ordered-list-interrupts-paragraph bug (destroys 200, prints 1., splits the sentence across three blocks) and literal backticks inside a bold run in follow-up 1 (the inline() alternation matches **...** first and never re-parses its contents). Neither blocked a ground-truth fact — the 503-for-three-hours-then-200 setup is legible in the Outcome — which is why this is a pass; but the first is a data-fidelity bug on live vault content and should be fixed before it eats a number that has no second copy on the page. Reader items 7-10 (what 3d 8h measures, no commit SHA/PR/diff stats/reviewer, no deploy or rollback facts for migration 0005, thin test detail) are absent from the vault record too, so they are scenario/schema gaps rather than screen bugs; the cheap win among them is labelling Duration as elapsed wall-clock.
